summary: #1530: local startup readiness and replay progress

replay.detail: Adds observation around existing startup and replay stages; it does not invalidate projections or introduce a new replay trigger. A full fallback still finishes its write transaction before API listeners bind; progress counts during base replay describe uncommitted work.

schema.detail: No database table, index, trigger or migration change in local startup readiness and replay progress; SQLite user_version is unchanged.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digest/drop policy are unchanged; this change adds no sealing coordination requirement.

compatibility.detail: On Linux, st doctor and st service status can read local startup readiness before the API exists. Doctor JSON adds startup. Announcing command clients return promptly after a failed connection during live full replay, while ordinary startup preserves --daemon-wait and long-lived drivers retain retries. macOS/non-Linux use existing API/outage checks; HTTP schemas and error codes are unchanged.

downtime.detail: Readiness reporting does not make the API available during recovery. Full replay can still cause a minutes-long interruption; no duration for an arbitrary populated store is established here. Inspect the local startup phase and daemon fallback log, then wait for API and projection health.

manual.detail: During an unavailable daemon on Linux, use st doctor or st service status to inspect the startup phase instead of treating service-manager active as API readiness. API_SOCKET.readiness.json and .readiness.lock are private rebuildable observations, not backup graph state; stale unlocked files are ignored.

recovery.detail: No additional recovery procedure introduced by this change. Preserve graph state, keys and configuration and follow the standard roll-forward guidance; this note does not qualify binary-only downgrade of the whole release.
